definition: Google AI Studio is a web-based integrated development environment developed by Google for prototyping applications using generative AI models.
details: Released in December 2023 alongside the Gemini API, the platform provides access to Google's Gemini family of models and related tools for image, video, and audio generation. The service targets both developers and non-technical users for testing prompts and generating code for the Gemini API.

explainer.lead: Google AI Studio is a browser-based workspace for trying ideas with Google's Gemini models and turning promising prompts into Gemini API code. It gives developers and non-technical users a quicker way to prototype generative AI applications without first building their own testing tools.

tiers.eli5: Google AI Studio is like a workbench for trying out AI ideas. You type instructions, see how a Gemini model responds, and adjust your instructions until they work better. When you are happy with the result, it can help create code so your own app can ask Gemini to do the same thing.
tiers.practitioner: Use the browser workspace to test prompts with Gemini models and related image, video, and audio generation tools, then generate code for the Gemini API to integrate into an application. Treat generated code and model outputs as starting points: test them in your own application rather than assuming a prototype is production-ready.
tiers.paperLevel: Google AI Studio is a web-based IDE whose prototyping workflow is prompt or tool configuration -> Gemini model experimentation -> Gemini API code generation. Released in December 2023 alongside the Gemini API, it supports application prototyping rather than defining a model, benchmark, or production-performance guarantee.

explainer.example: A developer prototypes a study helper by asking Gemini to explain a science topic at three reading levels, then tests the prompt with “Why is the sky blue?” After refining the instructions, the developer generates Gemini API code to use the prompt in an app.

explainer.intuition: It is a test bench between an idea and a finished AI application: experiment interactively first, then carry the working approach into code.
howItWorks: Enter and refine prompts for a Gemini model.
Try related image, video, or audio generation tools.
Generate code for the Gemini API.
Integrate and test that code in your application.
explainer.whyItMatters: It shortens the path from an AI idea to a working API prototype and makes prompt experimentation accessible to people who do not want to build an integration first.
misconceptions: It is a development tool, not an AI model itself.
It is not the Gemini API; it helps users experiment and generate code for that API.
A successful prototype does not make its outputs or generated code production-ready.

diagram.caption: Users refine prompts in AI Studio, test them with Gemini, and carry the result into an application through generated API code.
